target_customer: Consumer mobile gamers and social users; later web3 users who buy NFT avatars
problem: Pitched at YC as 'Minecraft meets Discord': a place to build and hang out in shared digital spaces. It later became an iOS social gaming app with user-made spaces.
business_model: Consumer app monetized through NFT avatar (Moji) sales on OpenSea
product_category: Social mobile metaverse and gaming app

founders.name: Benjamin South Lee
founders.background_notes: From the YC page. Joined Aave Companies as SVP of Product and Design after the Sonar acquisition (Decrypt). Also called Ben South Lee in press.

founders.name: Randolph Lee
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by Decrypt, which says he and Ben South Lee are brothers.

founders.name: Leo Cho
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; not named in acquisition coverage.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile app where users build and visit shared spaces needs real-time multiplayer and content tools, which is demanding but standard game engineering.

defensibility.rationale: User-created spaces and NFT avatars could create community ties, but Discord and Roblox-type platforms were far larger and coverage cites about 20,000 monthly users at most.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows these copying Sonar. The company instead sold to Aave Companies in December 2022 to build social apps on Lens Protocol.

market_need_then: Pandemic-era demand for online hangouts and Minecraft and Discord communities in 2020, though I found no company-specific demand data.

identity.mascot_or_character: Moji NFT avatars built from body, mouth, eyes and accessories with a gem rarity

branding.brand_signature: Sonar Moji NFT avatars with gem rarity tiers
branding.community_and_virality: Mojis sold on OpenSea; coverage mentions about 20,000 monthly active users per a press release shared with CoinDesk (per search summary, not opened).

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct avatar collectibles and acquisition press coverage, but the name is shared with many other products and usage was small.

pivots.from: Minecraft meets Discord for building and socializing
pivots.to: iOS social gaming app with user-made spaces and Moji NFT avatars, web3
pivots.why: Not stated; YC tags later include Crypto and Web3

outcome_analysis: Sonar started in Summer 2020 as a Minecraft-and-Discord style social space and became an iOS social metaverse app with NFT avatars. Aave Companies bought it on December 5, 2022 for an undisclosed price and the founders and two team members joined to build mobile social apps on Lens Protocol. Coverage frames the deal around the team, and no funding or traction beyond roughly 20,000 monthly users is sourced, so it reads as a team landing and not a verified product exit. YC lists the company as inactive.
notes: sonar.app returned HTTP 403, so the site was not read. Acquisition is stated by Decrypt and The Block (and a law firm note); YC directory status says Inactive, consistent with absorption into Aave. CB Insights Sonar pages with $2.5M and $750K could not be tied to this company and are not used. No funding found beyond the standard YC deal. No competitor source dated near 2020 was found, so that list is empty. The acquisition price is undisclosed. The pivot date is not given by sources.
